Resolves #20992

The dock's reload recreate now unlinks the destroyed predecessor from its container's stored vnode, the same unlink `Abstract#destroy` performs for a pane that still has a parent.

`commitRecreateCandidate` detaches the pane with `removeAt(index + 1, false)` before destroying it. The destroy then found no parent, and the container's vnode kept naming the pane until the container's own update landed. A workspace render landing in that window threw `Component not found` in `createMap`, which is the `DockReloadActionNL.spec.mjs:74` red on `dev` and on unrelated PRs. The insert-then-remove order stays as #18446 ruled.

Evidence: L3 (the real dock example in headless Chrome, under 6× CDP CPU throttle, locally) → L3 required (#20992 AC-3). Residual: none.

Prescription checked: `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/HeaderActions.mjs` owns the concern. It is the only `src` site that destroys a component it detached with `removeAt(…, false)`. `removeAt(…, false)` must keep the live reference, because its other callers move the item. `Abstract#destroy` cannot see a former parent.

| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockRecreateCandidate.spec.mjs`, "an ancestor render still maps through the container before its own update lands": after the commit, the slot holds the vnode the pane last rendered |

- **6× CPU throttle, dedicated-worker Neural Link path as in CI:** `DockReloadActionNL.spec.mjs` with `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` before boot (a local edit, not committed). With the fix it passed 10 of 10. On `dev` `c78adac361` it failed 3 of 5, each with `vdom update failed neo-dock-workspace-1 … Component not found for id: neo-dock-pane-2`.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Any synchronous `container.removeAt(index, false)` (or `remove(item, false)`) followed by `item.destroy()` bypasses `component.Abstract#destroy`'s parent-vnode unlink because `removeAt(..., false)` nulls `parentId` first; the caller must capture `{id, vnode}` before `destroy()` and invoke `VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(container.vnode, {[id]: vnode})` immediately after `destroy()` unregisters the component.
